summary: LLM inference costs are driven almost entirely by tokens processed, and most production systems overspend 2-5x by sending redundant context, over-using premium models, and ignoring caching. A combined strategy of prompt caching, semantic caching, model routing, prompt compression, and output constraints realistically cuts API spend 50-80% without degrading quality. Prompt caching alone is the highest-leverage, lowest-risk lever, cutting repeated-prefix input costs by up to 90%.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (Provider KV Cache)
techniques.description: Providers store the computed key-value tensors for a repeated static prompt prefix so the unchanged portion isn't reprocessed. The key is ordering prompts so static content (system instructions, few-shot examples, documents) comes first and dynamic content last.
techniques.savings: Up to 90% reduction on cached input tokens; studies show 41-80% total API cost reduction and 13-31% faster time-to-first-token
techniques.example: Place your 2,000-token system prompt and document context at the start of every request so Anthropic/OpenAI charge the discounted cached rate (often 10% of normal input cost) on repeated calls.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Caches responses based on embedding similarity rather than exact string match, so queries that 'mean the same thing' hit the cache. Requires careful similarity-threshold tuning to avoid returning confidently wrong answers.
techniques.savings: 30-50% cost reduction on conversational/FAQ workloads; 40-45% typical cache hit rate
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache so 'how do I cancel my subscription?' and 'cancel my plan how?' both return the same cached answer, set threshold to ~0.90 cosine similarity to minimize false hits.

techniques.name: Model Routing
techniques.description: Dynamically route each request to the cheapest model capable of handling its complexity, reserving premium models for genuinely hard tasks so cost scales with difficulty rather than volume.
techniques.example: Route 70% of traffic to a small model (e.g. GPT-4o-mini/Haiku), 25% to a mid model, and only 5% of complex reasoning tasks to a frontier model.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Instead of sending full context, send only relevant summaries or compressed representations. Tools like LLMLingua remove low-information tokens while preserving meaning, reducing input size.
techniques.example: Run retrieved documents through LLMLingua before injecting them into a RAG prompt, cutting a 4,000-token context to ~2,800 tokens with negligible quality loss.

techniques.name: Output Constraints / Max Tokens Control
techniques.description: Limit response length via max_tokens, structured output formats, and explicit instructions. Output tokens are often 2-4x more expensive than input tokens, so trimming them has outsized cost impact.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and prompt 'respond in JSON with only the fields requested' instead of letting the model produce verbose prose.

techniques.name: Reasoning-Length Budgeting
techniques.description: For reasoning/CoT models, control how many thinking tokens are spent using budget-signaling control tokens or self-estimated budgets, since reasoning tokens are billed and often excessive.
techniques.savings: 33-73% reasoning-token reduction at equal accuracy (IAPO ~36%, SelfBudgeter ~61%, Extra-CoT ~73% on MATH-500)
techniques.example: Apply BudgetThinker-style control tokens or set a reasoning-effort/thinking-budget parameter so the model solves a problem in ~1,000 instead of ~3,000 thinking tokens.

techniques.name: Retrieval / RAG Context Trimming
techniques.description: Retrieve and inject only the top-k most relevant chunks rather than entire documents, and re-rank to drop low-value passages before they consume context tokens.
techniques.example: Re-rank 20 retrieved chunks with a cross-encoder and pass only the top 3-5 into the prompt instead of dumping all 20.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Group multiple independent requests into batch API calls to access discounted asynchronous pricing (often ~50% off) for non-latency-sensitive workloads.
techniques.example: Submit overnight classification of 100k records via OpenAI's Batch API for 50% off standard token pricing.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library that stores LLM responses and serves them via embedding similarity, with pluggable vector stores and eviction policies.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source, self-hosted infra costs only)

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK across 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, model routing, fallback, rate limiting, and spend tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; LiteLLM Enterprise from ~$250+/mo for SSO, support, and governance

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing request logging, cost analytics, caching, and prompt management via a one-line proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k logs/mo); paid plans from ~$20/mo, usage-based scaling

tools.name: Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: Redis with vector search used as a low-latency semantic cache for LLM responses, integrated via LangChain/RedisVL.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source Redis free; Redis Cloud paid tiers from ~$5/mo, Enterprise custom

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Orchestration framework with built-in LLM caching (in-memory, SQLite, Redis, semantic), prompt templating, and routing utilities.

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression toolkit that removes low-information tokens from prompts to reduce input size while preserving output quality.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API gateway to hundreds of models with automatic routing, fallback, and transparent per-token pricing for cost-based model selection.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-as-you-go token pricing plus small routing margin; no subscription

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering semantic caching, routing, load balancing, guardrails, and observability across providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid plans from ~$49/mo plus enterprise

quick_wins: Enable provider prompt caching and reorder prompts so static system instructions and documents come first, dynamic content last — up to 90% off cached input tokens with zero quality loss.
Set max_tokens limits and request concise/structured output to cut expensive output tokens by up to 50%.
Route the majority of traffic to a cheaper small model (e.g. GPT-4o-mini or Claude Haiku) and reserve frontier models for the ~5% of genuinely hard requests.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) for FAQ/conversational workloads with a conservative ~0.90 similarity threshold to capture a 40%+ hit rate safely.
Trim RAG context to only the top 3-5 re-ranked chunks instead of injecting entire documents, cutting input tokens 30-60%.
